read.thesis: Chevron's Q3 was driven by refining margins and disciplined capex at the low end, with Permian held at a 1 MMboe/d plateau for capital efficiency; Venezuela adds self-funded barrels to 600,000 bpd by 2031.

utilisation.quote: achieved with a crude unit utilization rate of 98%.

capex.quote: we are trending towards the low end of the guidance this year

triggers.label: Permian capex/bbl down 25%
triggers.quote: we've seen a 25% reduction in CapEx per barrel

triggers.label: Refinery crude unit utilisation 98%
triggers.quote: achieved with a crude unit utilization rate of 98%

triggers.label: Refining margins elevated; 10% capacity offline
triggers.quote: the world has 10% of its refining capacity offline today

triggers.label: Working capital hit by late-quarter price rise
triggers.quote: Working capital was negatively impacted by sharp commodity prices increases late in the quarter.

triggers.label: Permian held at 1 MMboe/d plateau
triggers.quote: we're going to sustain this above 1 MMb of oil equivalent concept going forward

guidance.quote: finishing the year at the low end of our annual CapEx guidance
plans to double production for our three joint ventures to roughly 600,000 bpd, all on primary recovery, by 2031

guidance.value: Three to two rigs by year-end, 180,000 boe/d maintained
guidance.quote: We'll move from three rigs to two rigs at year-end while sustaining 180,000 bpd of oil equivalent production
we're increasing exploration spend by 50% relative to 2025
we intend to be buying back shares within that range
we are on track with Kilby to have first power in 2028 and full energization in 2031

red_flags.label: TCO contract extension unresolved; government asks
red_flags.quote: The list of issues has narrowed really to what I'd call the fundamental core issues

red_flags.label: Working capital drag from price spike
red_flags.quote: Working capital was negatively impacted by sharp commodity prices increases late in the quarter.

evasions.quote: I'm not going to comment on media reports or specifics
I don't want to speculate about what might take us back into a growth mode there
